Background and widget images are shrunk to screen size and re-encoded as WebP so they don't stall the page. With this on, that result is also kept on your device (encrypted, in internal storage) so it only has to be done once. Turn it off and images are still shrunk — they're just rebuilt each time you open the app, which is slower but stores nothing.

Time & Date

—
Automatic uses the timezone your device is already set to, so it needs no location permission and works offline.
Not synced
Your device clock is already kept accurate by your operating system, so leave this on "This device" unless you know it drifts. The time server is the only outbound request this app makes for the clock; if it fails, the device clock is used instead.

Privacy

Clears visit history, most-visited tiles and the Page Viewer's recent URLs. Notes, files, media, web apps, bookmarks, events and settings are kept.

Security

Encrypted at rest. Everything is stored encrypted with a per-device key. Set a master password and the sections you lock below are re-encrypted with a key derived from that password — so their contents can't be read from storage without it, and they're wiped from memory as soon as you close or auto-lock them.
No password set — locks are disabled.
When on, you must confirm the password (or passkey) before a note or folder can be locked — so a mistap can't lock you out of your own content.
When any locked section (Files, Media, Settings, etc.) is open and idle for this long, it will lock itself automatically.
When the app sits idle this long, every open section — modals, the note editor, the page viewer — closes and you're returned to the home screen.

External Links

This applies to links from bookmarks, history, most-visited, and clickable link elements throughout the app. The search bar always opens in a new tab, and links inside an article already open in the Page Viewer always stay in the viewer.
Choose what happens when you tap an article in the RSS list. Feed and article URLs are normalised to https:// automatically.
Thumbnails are fetched from the feed's own server. Turn this off to keep the list text-only — images then load only when you open an article.

Address Bar

On: anything that looks like a real address — example.com, site.co.uk, localhost:3000, file://…, an IP, or anything with a scheme — opens directly. Everything else, including things that merely contain a dot like kaim.ops, goes to your search engine. Off: Enter always searches and you use the Go button to open an address.

Page Viewer

On: pages you open in the viewer are recorded only in the viewer's own encrypted history and never appear in History, suggestions or Most Visited. Clearing browsing data still clears it.
Controls what the Page Viewer is allowed to render when opening a website. Images, text and typography formatting are always shown. Everything below is off by default — turning items on renders the real page and is progressively less isolated.
Enabling CSS or JavaScript switches the viewer to full-page mode: the site is rendered as-is inside a sandbox instead of extracted to a reader view.
event.preventDefault() lets a page block normal browser actions (link clicks, scrolling, key presses). It stays off unless you enable it here, even when JavaScript is allowed.

Notifications

One browser permission covers all three. Grant it once, then choose what you want to be notified about.
Alarms and the timer always show their in-app dialog and play a sound while Googoke is open. These add a system notification on top, which is what reaches you when the app is in the background.
Sounds
Built-in tone
Built-in beep
Pick any audio file from your Media (add one there first — Media now accepts audio alongside images and video). An individual alarm can override the alarm sound from its own editor. Leave these on the built-in tones and nothing is stored.

Item Timer

Time counter
Whether this task keeps an elapsed counter. What actually runs is decided by the job: start it from the top bar and the first unchecked task counts, including time when Googoke is closed. Checking it hands the clock to the next one.
A number on its own is read as minutes. The item is flagged when the counter passes the limit; nothing is deleted or reset.
Elapsed so far
—

Job Timing

How long the whole job may take. Counted only while the job is started — it does not run down while the job sits paused or before you begin. Accepts days and weeks as well as hours and minutes; a bare number means minutes.
If the job stays paused longer than this, you get a notification telling you to get back to it. Blank means it can sit paused indefinitely.
The job starts itself at this date and time and notifies you, the same way a reminder does. Leave blank to always start it by hand.
